newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HOLDERS PSG RATTLED IN TURKEY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HOLDERS PSG RATTLED IN TURKEY.

text.p: Defending champions Paris St Germain face the prospect of a second round exit from the Cup Winners' Cup after losing 4-2 to Turkey's Galatasaray in a roller-coaster match in Istanbul on Thursday.

The French league leaders, missing their Brazilian top-scorer Leonardo, fell 2-0 behind inside 15 minutes, recovered to 2-2 but were 4-2 down after 49 minutes and struggled to contain their opponents for the rest of the game.

The Turks, inspired by Romanian international midfielder Gheorghe Hagi, opened the scoring after five minutes of a frenetic first-half through striker Hakan Sukur and added a second through midfielder Tugay Kerimoglu nine minutes later.

The French did at least hit back with two vital away goals within two minutes from captain Paul Le Guen and Brazilian Julio Cesar to give themselves some hope for the second leg in Paris in a fortnight's time.
Galatasaray surged forward in search of more goals after Hakan Unsal had restored their two-goal advantage, but will still fancy their chances of progressing to the quarter-finals.
Elsewhere there were few surprises. Barcelona, among the favourites to usurp PSG's crown, came from behind to beat Red Star Belgrade 3-1 at Nou Camp while Fiorentina defeated Sparta Prague 2-1.

Brazilian Giovanni, thriving in the temporary absence of compatriot Ronaldo, scored Barcelona's first two goals before Portugal's Luis Figo rounded off a comfortable night for the Catalans, attempting to recapture a trophy they won twice in the 1980s.
In a rain-soaked Florence, Argentine Gabriel Batistuta honoured a pledge to his fans with an early goal, and Swedish midfielder Stefan Schwarz added the Italians' second after the interval.

Batistuta, who had not scored for a month and whose side have made a shaky start to the season, told supporters this week things were about to improve. "Fiorentina and Batistuta are just about to take off and the worst is behind us," he said.

Liverpool, like Barcelona, came from behind to win their tie against Swiss side Sion, and Portuguese league leaders Benfica beat Lokomotiv Moscow thanks to an eighth-minute goal from close-range by Joao Pinto.
